items.summary: Watchdog of the Constitution. Apex Ombudsman. Sentinel on the qui vive. Even as its monikers get more obscure, the role of the Supreme Court of India as the final protector of our rights has always been clear. That the Court has not always covered itself in glory while guarding the house we live in is, in its own words, a shame that deserves to be buried ten fathoms deep . Amidst reluctant whispers of the 'E' word (Emergency Lite, if you will) today, its ears surely must prick up. items.title: IP ownership in GCCs: Drafting, assignments, transfer pricing considerations and protection strategy
items.summary: Where a global capability centre (“GCC”) undertakes research and development for the multinational group that owns it (“Multinational Group”), ownership of the resulting intellectual property (“IP”) needs to be structured carefully, as the law does not treat all IP as a single category, nor in the same manner in all jurisdictions. For example, in India copyright in an employee’s work vests in the employer by statute, but an employee’s invention remains with the inventor unless assigned in writing. The procedure for transferring each type of IP may also differ. This, along with the intended role and value of the IP to the Multinational Group, should be considered so that the IP is secured, ownership suits the group’s operations, and the arrangement is tax compliant and efficient. A group planning to set up a GCC should settle its IP strategy first. While this article focuses on IP in India, the principles are largely universal. We have dealt mainly with copyright and patents, as these are most likely to arise in a GCC’s work, though the same approach applies to other IP. items.title: Calcutta High Court denies bail to ex-minister Sujit Bose in money laundering case
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court has rejected former West Bengal minister Sujit Bose's bail plea in a money laundering case linked to the alleged South Dum Dum municipality recruitment scam [Sujit Bose v. Directorate of Enforcement] Justice Tithankar Ghosh observed that Bose failed to meet the mandatory requirements for bail under Section 45 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). The Court also observed that no reasonable ground existed to believe that Bose was not guilty and was not likely to commit any other offence while on bail. It added that he cannot be released merely because the prosecution’s complaint stands filed and that the trial court has taken cognizance in the matter. "The Central Bureau of Investigation has also commenced further investigation after informing the Learned Special Court pursuant to receipt of information by the Enforcement Directorate. A vital stage of the investigation is in progress," the Court said in an order passed on October 13. According to the ED, various illegal municipal recruitments were carried out on recommendations received from Bose and other "politically exposed persons". items.title: Assembly ban imposed in Upper Siang, protesters detained under UAPA
items.summary: On October 11, the Upper Siang district administration issued an order prohibiting the assembly of five or more people amid intensifying protests against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP).
